About Event IAEOZ Summit 2025 Puerto Rico Prepare for the IAEOZ Summit 2025 Puerto Rico! Join us for three days of engaging sessions focusing on Agriculture and Energy sectors. KDM & Associates will host the 6th annual IAEOZ Summit on October 13-14, 2025 in San Juan, Puerto Rico.  The conference will be held in-person and livestreamed to a national and global audience. Local Puerto Rican business and government leaders, along with U.S. Federal officials and international experts in energy and agriculture, commerce, technology, and capital investment will discuss the changing role of farming, ranching, food production and distribution, and energy generation and supply.  A major focus will be on U.S. Government contracting opportunities available for local Minority Business Enterprises, and how their growth can contribute to building sustainable communities.  Puerto Rico represents a unique geographic and cultural crossroads between the continental United States and the Caribbean and Latin America, offering huge opportunities for expansion in trade and innovative technology transfer.  Moreover, nearly the entire island is designated as an ‘Opportunity Zone’ – providing special tax incentives for investment in industrial production and rural enterprises.  The Summit will spotlight, discuss and explore these opportunities, and lay the groundwork for new partnerships between local businesses, government authorities and investors.  Puerto Rico’s energy challenges have long been a critical topic of concern. From devastating hurricanes to an aging electrical grid, the island has faced consistent power outages and energy insecurity.  These issues have not only impacted daily life but have also slowed economic progress.  With the goal of achieving 40% renewable energy by 2025, the island is at a pivotal moment in its energy transition.  This shift presents immense opportunities for alternative energy solutions – especially ‘micro-grids’ dedicated to serving specific communities and industry clusters – to ensure that Puerto Ricans enjoy uninterrupted power, foster economic growth, and create a resilient energy system.  In the agribusiness sector, Summit speakers will share best practices on sustainability and carbon sequestration initiatives in farming, and examples of successful Minority-owned agribusiness enterprises.  Panelists will discuss Smart Farming, cutting-edge energy efficiency technologies in food production and food security, and strategies and programs to achieve rural community revitalization, job creation and workforce development.  Puerto Rico contains a good number of significant U.S. Military bases, with most bases located in relatively rural areas – and they continually purchase a broad scope of goods and services, many of which rural based businesses can readily supply, from food goods and produce to construction materials, and from facility maintenance, landscaping and utility upgrades to infrastructure engineering.  Summit speakers will discuss how the FPC can help enable Puerto Rican rural businesses learn about, bid and win upcoming procurement/contract opportunities being issued by the Military bases and commands in their respective locales.  The IAEOZ Summits have been strongly supported by the U.S. Dept. of Energy, Dept. of Agriculture, the National Science Foundation, and other Federal agencies including HUD, NASA, and the Dept. of Defense.  The FPC has edited video content from the Summit panels to produce a series of podcasts and training presentations, which have been disseminated to an even wider audience, including the 140-plus MBDA Minority Business Development Centers around the country, HBCUs, Hispanic Serving Institutions, and other key stakeholders nationally and overseas. sections.heading: Don Cravins Jr.
sections.content: Meet The Speakers Event Speakers Don Cravins Jr. President and CEO of the National Minority Supplier Development Council (NMSDC) × Don Cravins Jr. President and CEO of the National Minority Supplier Development Council (NMSDC) The Honorable Donald “Don” R. Cravins, Jr. is the Interim President and CEO of the National Minority Supplier Development Council (NMSDC) . A nationally recognized leader in public service, business development, and advocacy, he was named to the inaugural ForbesBLK 50 list for his impact and accomplishments. Previously, Don served as the nation’s first Under Secretary of Commerce for Minority Business Development , leading the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA) . Appointed in 2022 and unanimously confirmed by the U.S. Senate, he oversaw the agency’s expansion and its historic elevation into a permanent federal institution, supporting the country’s 9.7 million minority business enterprises. A graduate of Louisiana State University (B.A., Political Science) and the Southern University Law Center (J.D.) , Don began his career in elected office, serving in both the Louisiana House of Representatives and the Louisiana State Senate. Following Hurricanes Katrina and Rita, he became a strong advocate for business owners navigating recovery and rebuilding efforts. On Capitol Hill, he served as Staff Director and Chief Counsel for the U.S. Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship, where he helped craft and pass the landmark Small Business Jobs Act of 2010 . He later served as Chief of Staff to U.S. Senator Mary Landrieu of Louisiana. In addition to his civilian leadership, Don is a Lieutenant Colonel in the U.S. Army National Guard . He is a Life Meemerging businessr of Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. , The Rocks, Inc. , and the 100 Black Men of Prince George’s County . His honors include induction into the Southern University Law Center Hall of Fame , recognition as a Distinguished Alumnus of LSU , and being named Advocate of the Year by the National Bar Association in 2020. Don and his wife, Yvette Puckett Cravins, Esq. , have three children and reside in Maryland. Threads Bluesky LinkedIn Facebook Pinterest X (Twitter) Reddit × Jose F. Nino, Chairman, Biofriendly / CEO, El Niño Group, LLC × Jose F. Nino, Chairman, Biofriendly / CEO, El Niño Group, LLC José F. Niño – Business Strategist & Hispanic Business Advocate José F. Niño is a seasoned leader in national and international business development with over 30 years of experience advancing Hispanic-owned enterprises. As Chairman of Biofriendly / CEO, El Niño Group, LLC, he has led strategic planning, certification, and partnership development efforts across the U.S. and Latin America. He is also Co-founder of Allied Wireless Infrastructure Services (AWIS), a Hispanic-owned company delivering digital infrastructure solutions across North America. A former President and founding meemerging businessr of the U.S. Hispanic Chaemerging businessr of Commerce (USHCC), Niño helped grow its network from 30 to over 250 chaemerging businessrs, representing 1.3 million Hispanic-owned businesses. His efforts have empowered diverse entrepreneurs to access new markets and federal opportunities—most notably supporting a $50 billion telecom/IT contract for MicroTech. Niño currently chairs the Mid-Atlantic Hispanic Chaemerging businessr of Commerce and serves on several national boards focused on business, energy, and literacy. His legacy continues to influence inclusive economic development across the Americas. With 10 years within the APEX Accelerator system, Frank previously served as a procurement counselor and program manager for the Connecticut APEX Accelerator. He joined the NAPEX Board in 2019 and has held several key positions, including Region 1 Director, Strategic Planning Committee Chair, and currently serves as President-Elect. Frank brings over 20 plus years of senior-level leadership experience, with expertise in process improvement, operations and labor management across a variety of industries, including military, domestic and international business development, federal government defense contracting, aerospace manufacturing, nonprofit and governance operations, and higher education as an instructor in the Connecticut Community College System. A decorated U.S. Army Combat Veteran, Frank holds a certificate in Contract Negotiation from the Mattford Group and has earned degrees in Business Administration and Engineering & Operations Management Threads Bluesky LinkedIn Facebook Pinterest X (Twitter) Reddit × Keith Moore, Founder/CEO, KDM & Associates, LLC × Keith Moore, Founder/CEO, KDM & Associates, LLC Keith Moore – CEO, KDM & Associates, LLC & Founder, Open GovTV Keith Moore is a nationally recognized leader in government affairs, community development, and small business advocacy. As CEO of KDM & Associates and Founder of Open GovTV (OGTV), Moore leads a team dedicated to solving complex societal challenges through strategic partnerships and policy-driven innovation. With deep expertise in government contracting, public policy, and economic development, Moore has helped minority-owned firms secure billion-dollar opportunities and empowered underserved communities across the U.S. His career includes high-level appointments by the State of New Jersey, where he directed over $250 million in revitalization funds into Camden. OGTV, the nation’s first web platform to spotlight the White House’s Open Government Directive, extends KDM’s mission by promoting transparency, inclusion, and small business success in federal contracting. Through OGTV and KDM, Moore continues to champion inclusive growth and impactful solutions for government, business, and nonprofits. Threads Bluesky LinkedIn Facebook Pinterest X (Twitter) Reddit × Dr. Sidni L. Shorter, President & CEO, Utah Black Chaemerging businessr of Commerce × Dr. Sidni L. Shorter, President & CEO, Utah Black Chaemerging businessr of Commerce Dr. Sidni L. Shorter is a nationally recognized leader in economic development, nonprofit strategy, and equity-centered community transformation. As President and CEO of the Utah Black Chaemerging businessr of Commerce, she has led the Chaemerging businessr through record-breaking growth, including a 275% increase in meemerging businessrship and a 516% rise in contributions. She launched signature initiatives such as the Utah Black Wealth Conference and the Financial Capacity Program, expanding access to education, capital, and entrepreneurial support for underserved communities. Under her leadership, 100% of Chaemerging businessr meemerging businessrs who partnered with UBC on SBA loan applications were approved, demonstrating her commitment to economic empowerment and capital access. She is the former owner and CEO of ExecuteNow!, a finance and accounting firm that supported small businesses, nonprofits, and national clients such as Girl Scouts of America, NeighborWorks® America, and Dow Chemical. Her fundraising and organizational growth strategies helped raise millions and revolutionized how nonprofits engage with funders. Previously, she served as Deputy Director of the Louisiana Housing Alliance, helping develop 1,128 affordable homes and secure over $30 million in private construction financing following Hurricane Katrina. Dr. Shorter has been honored with the JP Morgan Chase 100 Women to KNOW in America (2024), Utah Business CEO of the Year (2023), and the Diamond Award for Excellence in Nonprofit Leadership (2024). She serves on the Zions Bank Board of Advisors, the Utah Governor's Talent, Education, and Industry Alignment Board, and the Westminster University Board of Trustees. She holds a doctorate in Biblical Psychology, a master's in theology, dual bachelor’s degrees in Behavioral Science and Theology, is  a Licensed Christian Therapist and recently earned a master’s degree in Business Management and Leadership. Dr. Shorter is known for her visionary strategy, collaborative leadership, and unwavering dedication to building ecosystems of opportunity, equity, and generational wealth. Woods, President of Public-Private Partnerships, Ready.net Scott D. Woods – President, Public-Private Partnerships, Ready.net Scott D. Woods is a nationally recognized broadband and telecommunications leader, currently serving as President of Public-Private Partnerships at Ready.net. With over 20 years of experience in broadband law, policy, and infrastructure deployment, he specializes in expanding connectivity through strategic public-private collaboration, federal funding, and community engagement. Previously, Scott served as the inaugural Director of the Office of Minority Broadband Initiatives at NTIA, where he played a critical role in implementing the $65 billion broadband expansion authorized by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. His leadership has empowered underserved communities through programs like the Broadband Technology Opportunities Program and the Connecting Minority Communities Pilot Program. A frequent keynote speaker and advisor to state, local, and national broadband coalitions, Scott is deeply committed to digital equity. He holds degrees from Morehouse College, American University, and Howard University School of Law, and serves on multiple advisory boards advancing broadband innovation nationwide.

Oscar L. Frazier – International Leadership Consultant & Growth Strategist Oscar L. Frazier is a globally respected consultant, speaker, and leadership trainer with over 20 years of experience transforming organizations through performance-driven leadership methodologies. A certified Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, PMP, and SAFe 5 Agilist, Oscar specializes in growth strategy, innovation, and team empowerment—particularly within the federal and corporate sectors. He has successfully managed multimillion-dollar consulting portfolios, owned businesses across diverse industries, and trained leaders in over 10 countries across Africa, Europe, and the U.S. His agility-based and human-centered leadership frameworks have empowered organizations like IBM, Booz Allen Hamilton, the VA, and CMS to drive tangible results. Oscar is also a Forbes-published author and thought leader, known for his book “Confessions: The Truth About Perfect Timing.” With roots in Charleston, SC, and a career marked by resilience and impact, Oscar brings unorthodox, high-impact strategies that resonate from the C-suite to frontline teams worldwide.

Ramiro A. Cavazos – President & CEO, United States Hispanic Chaemerging businessr of Commerce Ramiro A. Cavazos is the President and CEO of the United States Hispanic Chaemerging businessr of Commerce (USHCC), the largest Hispanic business advocacy organization in America. A seasoned economic development expert, Cavazos has spent decades championing bipartisan solutions that promote entrepreneurship, innovation, and wealth creation for all Americans. Previously, he led the San Antonio Hispanic Chaemerging businessr of Commerce, driving international trade missions and leading the chaemerging businessr to 5-Star accreditation. His public service includes leadership roles in the City of San Antonio and the University of Texas Health Science Center, where he advanced technology and business development partnerships. Cavazos brings private-sector experience from Levi Strauss & Co. and 15 years as a bank director. He’s a widely respected voice on Latino business issues and a meemerging businessr of the Council on Foreign Relations. A 7th generation Texan, Cavazos is a national thought leader whose insights have shaped U.S. policy, global trade, and inclusive economic growth.
